stem: A client self-administers insulin at home. Which instruction about used needles is appropriate?

options.A: Recap used needles with two hands and then place them loose in household trash after verifying that each cap is secure.
options.B: Flush used needles down the toilet after injection so household members and sanitation workers cannot contact the sharps.
options.C: Keep used needles on an uncovered rigid tray until several have accumulated, then transfer the group into household trash.
options.D: Place each used needle promptly into an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container when available and follow local disposal requirements when the container is ready for removal.

rationale: FDA recommends placing used needles and other sharps in a sharps disposal container immediately after use. FDA-cleared containers are preferred when available, and when the container is about three-quarters full, community guidelines should be followed for disposal. Loose sharps should not be placed in household/public trash or flushed down the toilet. D is correct.
educational_objective: Teach home users to place used needles immediately into an appropriate sharps container and dispose of the filled container according to local/community requirements.
source_document_title: Best Way to Get Rid of Used Needles and Other Sharps
source_version_date: Current FDA consumer guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Step 1: place all needles and other sharps in a sharps disposal container immediately after use. Step 2: dispose of used sharps containers according to community guidelines. FDA Sharps Disposal Containers page: FDA-cleared containers are recommended; appropriate heavy-duty household containers may be alternatives when cleared containers are unavailable.
source_claim_supported: Used home injection needles should be placed immediately into an appropriate sharps disposal container, preferably FDA-cleared when available, and the container should be disposed of according to local/community requirements.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: handle biohazardous materials safely, protect from injury, and provide safety/infection-prevention teaching.

source_original.source_detail: Step 1: Place all needles and other sharps in a sharps disposal container immediately after they have been used. FDA page currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Overview of Content — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: infection prevention, biohazard handling, security plans, equipment safety and workplace safety. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the home-sharps construct and key D. Added 'when available' so the final teaching remains accurate when FDA-cleared containers are unavailable and an acceptable heavy-duty household alternative is permitted by local guidance.

audit_findings.source_authority: FDA primary consumer medical-device guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: FDA disposal Step 1 and Step 2; Sharps Disposal Containers alternative-container guidance
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately prioritizes immediate container placement and local disposal rules without falsely implying an FDA-cleared container is the only permissible option in every locality.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because loose sharps should not be placed in household trash and two-handed recapping creates sharps risk.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because FDA says never flush loose sharps down the toilet.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because sharps should be placed into the disposal container immediately after use.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D provides the recommended immediate safe-disposal sequence.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are concrete disposal behaviors; D is supported by the FDA process rather than wording cues.
audit_findings.blueprint: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — biohazard/sharps safety and teaching.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current FDA home-sharps pages, all alternatives, rationale, objective and NCSBN Safety mapping. D remained uniquely correct.
